about.description:
pixi is a cross-platform, multi-language package manager and workflow tool build on the shoulders of the conda ecosystem.

pixi provides all developers the exceptional experience that is usually found with package managers like cargo or yarn but for any language.

# Highlights

- Support for multiple languages like Python, C++ and R using Conda packages
- All OS's: Linux, Windows, macOS (including Apple Silicon)
- A lockfile is always included and always up-to-date.
- A clean and simple Cargo-like command-line interface.
- Install tools per-project or system-wide.
- Completely written in Rust and build on top of the rattler library.
about.summary: pixi is a cross-platform, multi-language package manager and workflow tool build on the shoulders of the conda ecosystem.

script.content:
$env.OPENSSL_DIR = $env.PREFIX

if $nu.os-info.name == "windows" {
  # Avoid long path issues
  let drive = ($env.SRC_DIR | path split | first)  # e.g. "D:"
  $env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR = $"($drive)\\cb"  # D:\cb
  $env.CARGO_HOME = $"($drive)\\ch"        # D:\ch
}

if $nu.os-info.name == "linux" {
  # This flag is needed for tree-sitter on linux
  $env.CFLAGS = $"($env.CFLAGS) -D_BSD_SOURCE"
}

# `zstd` is a build dependency of `uv-python`, so cargo compiles the
# `zstd-sys` C sources for the build platform too. cc-rs accumulates
# the flags of `CFLAGS` into both compiles, which makes the build platform
# compiler choke on the target's `-march=core2` / `-mabi=lp64d`. Pass them
# via `TARGET_CFLAGS` instead, which cc-rs only applies to the target compile.
if ${{ "true" if unix and build_platform != target_platform else "false" }} {
  $env.TARGET_CFLAGS = $env.CFLAGS
  hide-env CFLAGS
}

# On win-arm64, `CC=cl.exe` resolves to the ARM64-targeting cl.exe, so the
# build platform `zstd-sys` objects come out ARM64 and the x64 build script
# fails to link. cc-rs ignores `CC_FOR_BUILD`, so forward it explicitly.
if ${{ "true" if win and build_platform != target_platform else "false" }} {
  $env.CC_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc = $env.CC_FOR_BUILD
  $env.CXX_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc = $env.CXX_FOR_BUILD
}

# aws-lc-sys's cc builder only switches to clang-cl on win-arm64 when `CC`
# is unset, but the activation sets `CC=cl.exe`. cl.exe ignores the `.S`
# assembly, so linking fails on missing objects. The cmake builder
# assembles them with clang-cl.
if ${{ "true" if target_platform == "win-arm64" else "false" }} {
  $env.AWS_LC_SYS_CMAKE_BUILDER = "1"
}

# PGO needs to run the instrumented binary, so the script falls back to a
# regular release build when cross-compiling. win-arm64 skips PGO because
# instrumented builds are broken on that target:
# https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/156675
let pgo = if ${{ "false" if target_platform == "win-arm64" else "true" }} { ["--pgo"] } else { [] }
let executable = if $nu.os-info.name == "windows" { "pixi.exe" } else { "pixi" }
(^python ($env.SRC_DIR | path join scripts build_pgo.py)
  --target $env.CARGO_BUILD_TARGET
  --no-default-features --features native-tls
  --auditable
  ...$pgo
  --output ($env.PREFIX | path join bin $executable))
cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output $"($env.SRC_DIR)/THIRDPARTY.yml"

if $nu.os-info.name != "windows" {
  # Generate shell completions for unix shells
  let pixi = $"($env.PREFIX)/bin/pixi"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/bash-completion/completions"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/zsh/site-functions"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/fish/vendor_completions.d"
  ^$pixi completion --shell bash | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/bash-completion/completions/pixi"
  ^$pixi completion --shell zsh | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/zsh/site-functions/_pixi"
  ^$pixi completion --shell fish | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/fish/vendor_completions.d/pixi.fish"
}

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler("c") }}
    - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
    - ${{ compiler("rust") }}
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
    - cargo-auditable
    - cargo-bundle-licenses
    - cmake
    - nushell
    # A version constraint keeps python out of the build variants.
    - python >=3.10
    - pkg-config
    - if: unix
      then: make
    - if: osx
      then: ld64
  host:
    # native-tls links openssl on linux (macOS uses Security.framework,
    # Windows uses schannel, neither needs a host dependency)
    - if: linux
      then: openssl

tests:
  - script:
      - pixi --help
  - package_contents:
      strict: true
      bin:
        - pixi
      files:
        - if: unix
          then:
            - share/bash-completion/completions/pixi
            - share/zsh/site-functions/_pixi
            - share/fish/vendor_completions.d/pixi.fish

about:
  summary: pixi is a cross-platform, multi-language package manager and workflow tool build on the shoulders of the conda ecosystem.
  description: |
    pixi is a cross-platform, multi-language package manager and workflow tool build on the shoulders of the conda ecosystem.

    pixi provides all developers the exceptional experience that is usually found with package managers like cargo or yarn but for any language.

    # Highlights

    - Support for multiple languages like Python, C++ and R using Conda packages
    - All OS's: Linux, Windows, macOS (including Apple Silicon)
    - A lockfile is always included and always up-to-date.
    - A clean and simple Cargo-like command-line interface.
    - Install tools per-project or system-wide.
    - Completely written in Rust and build on top of the rattler library.

  license: BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - THIRDPARTY.yml
  homepage: https://pixi.prefix.dev
  repository: https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - lucascolley
    - wolfv
    - baszalmstra
    - tdejager
    - ruben-arts
    - Hofer-Julian

script.content:
$env.OPENSSL_DIR = $env.PREFIX

if $nu.os-info.name == "windows" {
  # Avoid long path issues
  let drive = ($env.SRC_DIR | path split | first)  # e.g. "D:"
  $env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR = $"($drive)\\cb"  # D:\cb
  $env.CARGO_HOME = $"($drive)\\ch"        # D:\ch
}

if $nu.os-info.name == "linux" {
  # This flag is needed for tree-sitter on linux
  $env.CFLAGS = $"($env.CFLAGS) -D_BSD_SOURCE"
}

# `zstd` is a build dependency of `uv-python`, so cargo compiles the
# `zstd-sys` C sources for the build platform too. cc-rs accumulates
# the flags of `CFLAGS` into both compiles, which makes the build platform
# compiler choke on the target's `-march=core2` / `-mabi=lp64d`. Pass them
# via `TARGET_CFLAGS` instead, which cc-rs only applies to the target compile.
if ${{ "true" if unix and build_platform != target_platform else "false" }} {
  $env.TARGET_CFLAGS = $env.CFLAGS
  hide-env CFLAGS
}

# On win-arm64, `CC=cl.exe` resolves to the ARM64-targeting cl.exe, so the
# build platform `zstd-sys` objects come out ARM64 and the x64 build script
# fails to link. cc-rs ignores `CC_FOR_BUILD`, so forward it explicitly.
if ${{ "true" if win and build_platform != target_platform else "false" }} {
  $env.CC_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc = $env.CC_FOR_BUILD
  $env.CXX_x86_64_pc_windows_msvc = $env.CXX_FOR_BUILD
}

# aws-lc-sys's cc builder only switches to clang-cl on win-arm64 when `CC`
# is unset, but the activation sets `CC=cl.exe`. cl.exe ignores the `.S`
# assembly, so linking fails on missing objects. The cmake builder
# assembles them with clang-cl.
if ${{ "true" if target_platform == "win-arm64" else "false" }} {
  $env.AWS_LC_SYS_CMAKE_BUILDER = "1"
}

# PGO needs to run the instrumented binary, so the script falls back to a
# regular release build when cross-compiling. win-arm64 skips PGO because
# instrumented builds are broken on that target:
# https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/156675
let pgo = if ${{ "false" if target_platform == "win-arm64" else "true" }} { ["--pgo"] } else { [] }
let executable = if $nu.os-info.name == "windows" { "pixi.exe" } else { "pixi" }
(^python ($env.SRC_DIR | path join scripts build_pgo.py)
  --target $env.CARGO_BUILD_TARGET
  --no-default-features --features native-tls
  --auditable
  ...$pgo
  --output ($env.PREFIX | path join bin $executable))
cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output $"($env.SRC_DIR)/THIRDPARTY.yml"

if $nu.os-info.name != "windows" {
  # Generate shell completions for unix shells
  let pixi = $"($env.PREFIX)/bin/pixi"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/bash-completion/completions"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/zsh/site-functions"
  mkdir $"($env.PREFIX)/share/fish/vendor_completions.d"
  ^$pixi completion --shell bash | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/bash-completion/completions/pixi"
  ^$pixi completion --shell zsh | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/zsh/site-functions/_pixi"
  ^$pixi completion --shell fish | save --force $"($env.PREFIX)/share/fish/vendor_completions.d/pixi.fish"
}
